In 1958, after some 54 years on the market, all vacant and unclaimed Ceded Strip land was returned to tribal ownership. Section 1 of the Act of May 19, 1958 (72 Stat. 121) states: "All lands now or hereafter classified as vacant and undisposed-of ceded lands on the following Indian reservations [5, including Crow] are hereby restored to tribal ownership, subject to valid existing rights." 10,260.95 acres of land were thus returned to trust status. The lands returned to tribal surface ownership amounted to less than 3 percent of the original 1,100,000 acres; about 14 percent of the coal reserves were contained in these lands. In addition, mineral rights had been retained by the U.S. Government when the lands in the Ceded Area were patented to the settlers; these mineral rights were also returned to Crow Tribal ownership in 1958. The Crow coal rights in the Ceded Area now total just over 150,000 acres, of which 30,876 acres are in the Westmoreland Resources lease area involved in this study. These coal rights are owned in trust by the Crow Indians and are administered for the Secretary of Interior by the Bureau of Indian Affairs.
Surface ownership of the 1,100,000 acres in the Ceded Area presently includes approximately 9,000 acres of tribal land, 17,000 acres of
allotted land, 45,000 acres of State land, and over 1,000,000 acres of
private fee land. In other words, over 90 percent of the surface acreage in the Ceded Area consists of fee land, and approximately four
percent is in Indian ownership.
